strings.about.title: About
strings.about.tagline: SNMP-based traffic monitoring for peering and transit networks.
strings.about.intro: Bifrost polls interface counters over SNMP, stores the raw data in TimescaleDB, and works out rates when they are read. Traffic is shown in total and broken down by role and counterparty — IX, PNI, CDN, transit, peering and customer.
strings.about.license.own: The technique and the way we put together the Distribution page and how it is presented, as well as the map module, are developed in-house. For the map module, the algorithm behind it — and how we select objects and connect them to each other — is part of what we regard as our own algorithm and design.

See LICENSE in the source code.

strings.setting.snmp_community.label: SNMP community (default)
strings.setting.snmp_community.help: Default SNMP v1/v2c community. Used when you give no community while discovering a host, and then stored on the host. A change applies to new hosts, not existing ones. Default «public».
strings.setting.ospf_proto.label: OSPF version (logical map)
strings.setting.ospf_proto.help: Which OSPF version is mapped. v2 (default, verified). v3/both use OSPFV3-MIB — UNTESTED until tried against real v3 equipment.
strings.setting.ospf_ref_bw.label: OSPF reference bandwidth (Gbps)
strings.setting.ospf_ref_bw.help: Used to tell automatic OSPF cost (ref-bw ÷ link speed) from cost set by hand on the logical map. Default 1000 (= 1000G). Set it to your network's actual reference bandwidth.
strings.setting.flow_max_paths.label: Traffic flow: number of paths
strings.setting.flow_max_paths.help: How many of the largest traffic flows the «Traffic flow» overlay highlights on the physical map. Default 3. Hard limit 2–6 — the point is to show the largest, not everything.
strings.setting.mpls_lsp.label: MPLS LSP collection (logical map)
strings.setting.mpls_lsp.help: Collect MPLS LSPs over SNMP (MPLS-TE-MIB) so «OSPF+LSP» routing on the logical map can show the actual LSP paths. Best effort, UNTESTED against real equipment — off by default. Demo/MOCK always shows example LSPs regardless of this.
strings.setting.mpls_lsp_max_rows.label: MPLS LSP — max rows per router
strings.setting.mpls_lsp_max_rows.help: Protection against overload: the LSP SNMP walk stops after this many rows per router. Default 500. Raise it if you need more LSPs; lower it if the routers notice the load.
strings.setting.snmp_cooldown_min.label: SNMP cooldown per router (min)
strings.setting.snmp_cooldown_min.help: Minimum time between on-demand SNMP queries to the SAME router (rebuild OSPF/LSP, re-scan) — global, whoever triggers them and from where. Default 1 min, minimum 1. The scheduled poller is exempt.
strings.setting.http_cooldown_min.label: External HTTP cooldown (min)
strings.setting.http_cooldown_min.help: Minimum time between on-demand calls to the SAME external service (e.g. NetBox sync) — global, whoever triggers them and from where. Default 1 min, minimum 1.
strings.setting.max_interface_speed_mbps.label: Max interface speed / rate cap (Mbps)
strings.setting.max_interface_speed_mbps.help: This number is used in three places: (1) the highest speed you can enter on an interface (catches typos); (2) the «impossible rate» limit — a measured rate above it is treated as a counter glitch and shown as a gap in the graph, not as a spike; (3) together with the factor below it forms the cap «Clean up Peaks» uses for aggregated records. Default 10 000 000 (= 10 Tbps).
strings.setting.peak_aggregate_factor.label: Rate cap factor (×)
strings.setting.peak_aggregate_factor.help: One factor applied in two places: (1) per interface — a measured rate above the interface's speed × this factor is treated as a glitch and shown as a gap (set high enough for over-subscription and bursts to show normally); (2) for «Clean up Peaks» — the aggregate cap = max interface speed × this. Default 7 (valid 1–100).
strings.setting.max_map_nodes.label: Max nodes per map
strings.setting.max_map_nodes.help: Upper limit for the number of nodes in one map. Enforced when nodes are added (auto maps too) and when saving. Default 100.
strings.setting.max_bg_tiles.label: Max map tiles per snapshot
strings.setting.max_bg_tiles.help: Upper limit for how many map tiles a snapshot of the background map may fetch. Larger areas are refused with a message to zoom out. Default 400.
strings.setting.netbox_url.label: NetBox URL
strings.setting.netbox_url.help: Base URL of NetBox (e.g. https://netbox.example.net). Used to fetch the site + GPS position of each device, so maps can place the routers geographically. Checked against NetBox when you save.
strings.setting.netbox_token.label: NetBox API token
strings.setting.netbox_token.help: API token for NetBox (read-only is enough). Stored as a secret; never shown again. The URL + token are checked with a real request to NetBox when you save.
strings.setting.netbox_verify_tls.label: NetBox: verify the TLS certificate
strings.setting.netbox_verify_tls.help: «off» turns OFF certificate verification towards NetBox (for internal instances with a self-signed certificate). Leave it «on» when NetBox has a valid certificate.

strings.setting.flow_overlay.help: Experimental traffic flow overlay (the river model) on the physical map. Hidden by default — the feature is not good enough yet (BETA). «on» shows the «Traffic flow (BETA)» button in the map view.

strings.dq.sub: rate cap, glitch clean-up and Peaks maintenance
strings.dq.intro: This page is for keeping the traffic data clean. Bifrost works out rates from raw counters, and a counter glitch, an ifIndex reshuffle or a capacity step on a LACP/AE interface can give one reading with an impossible jump — a false spike in graphs and Peaks. The protection is automatic (a rate cap per interface hides the impossible as a gap), but the individual bad readings are still in the raw data. Here you find and fix them, adjust the rate cap itself, and rebuild Peaks if an old false record is still there.
strings.dq.fix_title: Set the reading to the average of its neighbours (keeps the volume)
strings.dq.delete_title: Remove the reading — the rate spans the gap
strings.dq.ack_title: Known/handled — hide from the list without deleting raw data (reversible)
strings.dq.none: No readings above {thr} Gbps in the last {days} days.
strings.dq.help_fix_html: Fix — sets the reading's counters to the average of the readings before and after. The total volume is kept (the real volume is split evenly over the two intervals). Right for a single bad reading (an isolated spike). Needs a valid neighbouring reading on each side.
strings.dq.help_delete_html: Delete — removes the reading; the rate then spans the gap. Right when several readings in a row are broken (a cluster), when the jump spans a gap (reset/restart/restore) or after a lasting capacity change — there interpolation makes no sense.
strings.dq.help_ack_html: Leave — «looks wrong, but is already handled». Mark it as known and hide it from the list without touching raw data. Recommended when the rate is already above the rate cap (hidden automatically in graphs/Peaks) — typically a counter step from a capacity change that Delete could not remove cleanly anyway. Reversible (undo at the bottom).
strings.dq.help_star_html: ★ = the recommended action for the diagnosis. None of them harm other data, and all are recorded in the Log. Peaks and graphs are healed automatically in the background after Fix/Delete.
strings.dq.purge_title: Rebuild Peaks from (filtered) data — runs in the background
strings.dq.purge_hint: Rebuilds the all-time records from filtered data and removes impossible aggregate peaks. Peaks never go down by themselves, so an old false record stays until you clean up. Runs in the background.
strings.dq.cap_summary_html: Rate cap (advanced) — the same values as under Settings
strings.dq.cap_intro: The cap decides what counts as an impossible rate and is hidden as a gap. Set it high enough for legitimate over-subscription and bursts to show, but low enough to catch glitches. The change applies everywhere at once.
strings.dq.cap_presets_hint: Pick a preset from the list, or type freely (spaces as in «50 000 000» are fine).
strings.dq.cap_rule_html: Per interface: a rate above speed × factor = glitch (gap). Unknown speed → a flat backstop cap (the max above). «Clean up Peaks» uses max × factor as the aggregate cap.
